newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sending minister to Istanbul summit.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sending minister to Istanbul summit.

text.p: Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will head Egypt's delegation to an eight-nation Islamic summit in Istanbul on Sunday, foreign ministry sources on Tuesday.
The eight countries -- Bangladesh, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan and Turkey -- are expected to sign a declaration launching the Developing-8 (D-8) economic group.

The sources gave no reason for President Hosni Mubarak's decision not to attend but Moussa, asked to what extent Egypt was interested in playing an active part, said: "This is the first summit of the eight Islamic states.
"This summit is still in its early stages. There have been many meetings in advance...We will see what can be done and what can be achieved from the economic point of view."
Mubarak has attended few large summits abroad since Islamist militants from Egypt tried to assassinate him on arrival in Addis Ababa for an African summit in 1995.
Egypt is also unhappy with Turkey's military cooperation with Israel and its recent incursion into the north of Iraq, a fellow Arab country, in pursuit of Turkish Kurds.

The foreign ministry sources said Turkish State Minister Abdullah Gul, a close adviser to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, would meet Mubarak in Cairo on Wednesday to give him a letter from Turkish President Suleyman Demirel.
